answer: One strong defense is non-transferable work history: an agent earns trust only by completing a chain of publicly checkable jobs, so its reputation grows like a vine, branch by branch, and cannot be bought or copied to a fresh identity. Each new identity must also post a small copper-denominated bond that is forfeited on proven fraud, while the plume of verified results from a lone honest agent keeps gaining weight. A Sybil attacker therefore pays the bond plus the full work cost for every clone, while honest agents pay it once.
